title: check-kb-bible-drift: owned entries judged against the merge-base, one-line restamp, git-decided uncommitted, run in CI
summary: scripts/check-kb-bible-drift.mjs compares the bible committed at HEAD with the one at merge-base(HEAD, --base). An entry is branch-owned if that base bible lacks it or has a different version, so a base that moved after the last merge never makes the branch own entries it did not touch. Owned entries whose cited files' HEAD blob ids differ from source_file_hashes make it exit 1 and print the exact --restamp command; --restamp refuses only when git diff HEAD shows a real change to the bible (CRLF checkouts are fine) and writes LF exporter format. ci.yml runs it on pull requests.

title: Only roles with a kb-apply post-result step have their kb_captures recorded; the KB block no longer promises it to others
summary: A dispatched role kb_captures output is applied only if its role-policies.mjs row lists kb-apply in postResult; planner, plan-reviewer, scoped-replan roles, deployer, integ-test-runner and regression-test-runner have none. The agent() wrapper now passes captureChannel=agentTypeAppliesKbCaptures(agentType) to kbKnowledgeBlock, so those roles are told to note findings in their own report instead of being promised the orchestrator records kb_captures; a persona shared across rows counts as no channel unless every row has kb-apply.

title: Post-harvest bible recheck reports unreachable maintainer ids as unchecked with a generic WARN
summary: With noReviewLeft, recheckSprintBible removes ids that never reached kb_bible_commit from the confirmations queue and reports them in out.unchecked with a WARN saying the entries may carry a drifted basis and need re-checking before the branch merges. The WARN names no repository-specific script (the engine is generic). Removing them keeps the end-of-run pending-confirmations warning from calling them unpublished, since they are already on the branch bible.

title: Setup shell's $$ is unsafe to record for liveness checks under Git Bash on Windows
summary: scripts/sandbox-lock.mjs's acquire CLI previously recorded the Setup shell's self-reported $$, which under Git Bash on Windows is an MSYS-internal pid invisible to defaultDeps.isAlive's native process.kill(pid,0) check -- fixed by having the CLI record its own process.ppid instead, since the CLI process is itself a direct child of the Setup shell and process.ppid always resolves in the native OS pid namespace.

title: New fleet-sprint *.mjs/*.js files must be registered in GUARDED_MODULES or the apra-fleet-se suite fails
summary: Every *.mjs/*.js file under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/ (recursive) must be listed in GUARDED_MODULES or GUARD_REGISTRATION_EXEMPT in fleet-sprint/guarded-modules.mjs. guarded-modules-coverage.test.mjs enforces this. A miss makes CI's "Run tests" exit 1 while every vitest and node --test summary still shows 0 failures; the only visible signal is the line "> apra-fleet-se suite FAILED (exit 1)".

title: bd prints literal JSON null, not [], for an empty dolt remote list
summary: `bd dolt remote list --json` emits the JSON literal null when no Dolt remotes are configured. parseDoltRemoteList maps that to [] before its non-array guard, so an unwired repo reads as "no remotes" rather than a parse error; every other non-array shape still throws. Without the null branch, checkDoltRemoteAbsent returns ok:false ("could not parse") for a repo that is simply not wired to a Dolt remote.

title: Member mixed-tier KB read: bible half first, per-side limit, own CONFIRMED excluded
summary: getMemberSplitRead (kb-self.ts) splits a MEMBER tier list naming CONFIRMED plus another tier: CONFIRMED from the checkout bible view plus untagged global, other tiers from the per-repo DB plus global with owner tag member:<uuid>. kb_query merges bible-first per side (project, global) and limits per side, so l1_results can exceed limit; own CONFIRMED rows in the per-repo DB are never returned.

title: Lane order ignores containers: lowerOrderLaneMates is the single lane-mate rule
summary: beads-scope.mjs lowerOrderLaneMates computes a bead's open lower-order lane-mates (same metadata.streak, lower finite streakOrder) and never counts a container (any bead that is the .parent of another bead in the list, per containerIdsOf). unmetPrerequisites, partitionReadyByGoal and worklists.mjs holdBackByLaneOrder all call it; classifyBlockedReport inherits it via unmetPrerequisites.

title: A post-harvest drop of an entry this branch alone added is removed with no tombstone
summary: After recheckSprintBible(noReviewLeft) commits a drift withdrawal, liftOwnTombstones reads the bible at the merge-base (createBaseBibleIds in runner.js) and queues a restore for each dropped id the base bible does not carry, so the withdrawn tombstone does not block that id from re-merging later. An id the base carries keeps its withdrawal. An unreadable base keeps every withdrawal.

title: gitRepos is an access list; only a single URL-shaped entry is a usable origin
summary: agent.gitRepos is declared optional string[] and usually holds bare "Owner/Repo" access identifiers, not clone URLs. knownRepoRemoteUrl (in src/services/member-remote-url.ts, re-exported from execute-prompt.ts) returns a URL only when gitRepos has EXACTLY one entry AND it is URL-shaped (contains "://" or starts with "git@"); anything else yields undefined rather than a guessed URL.

title: kb_query files/symbols cited filter is a hard SQL filter gated by query_filters over http
summary: kb_query files/symbols are a hard filter (cited-filter.ts) applied in SqliteProvider.query next to the tag filter. HttpKbProvider forwards them only when GET /api/kb/capabilities lists them in the optional query_filters field and otherwise throws E-KB-HTTP-UNSUPPORTED before sending. kb_query re-applies the filter (entryCites) only to answers from non-SQLite providers.

title: kb_import keeps bible ids on every AUDN path; duplicates resolve via bible_id_aliases
summary: Under importMode, SqliteProvider.capture stores linked ('update') and flagged imports under the bible id when it is free. A bible entry deduplicated ('none') records a bible_id_aliases row pointing at the local row that absorbed it. applyTombstoneToRow resolves through that alias when no row has the id, so kb_import tombstones and POST /api/kb/withdraw reach the row.
